intended_object: The predicate says that the data (μ, a, b) is a Lévy–Khintchine-type (Stieltjes) representation of a complete Bernstein function f: on [0, ∞), f(t) = a + b t + ∫_{(0,∞)} t/(t+x) σ(dx), with a, b ≥ 0 and σ a measure on (0, ∞) such that ∫ (1+x)⁻¹ dσ < ∞ (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, Theorem 6.2). This is read off the docstring, the module documentation and the cited reference.
explanation:
The definition unfolds to three conditions:
- μ{0} = 0;
- the weight (1+x)⁻¹ is integrable for μ;
- f equals a + b t + ∫ t/(t+x) dμ(x) at every t ≥ 0.

Here μ is a measure on ℝ≥0 with no atom at 0, which is the same thing as a measure σ on (0, ∞), and this is the setting of SSV Theorem 6.2. The weight (1+x)⁻¹ is continuous and positive, so it is measurable, and integrability is exactly the condition ∫ (1+x)⁻¹ dσ < ∞.

The Bochner integral raises no junk-value problem. For t > 0 the integrand satisfies 0 ≤ t/(t+x) ≤ max(1, t)·(1+x)⁻¹, so it is integrable. At t = 0 the integrand is identically 0 (using 0/0 = 0 at x = 0). So f(0) = a, which matches the usual continuous extension f(0+) = a.

The coefficients a, b are in ℝ≥0, as required. Only the values of f on [0, ∞) are constrained, which matches functions defined on [0, ∞) or (0, ∞) in the literature.

The real half-line is the natural setting for this notion, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no notion of Bernstein or complete Bernstein functions.
